---
title: "For Instructors"
subtitle: "Reproducible, hardware-independent problem sets, paired with the lecture decks for Volumes I and II."
---

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import mlsysim
from mlsysim.physics import calc_kv_cache_size

Engine = mlsysim.Engine
_resnet = mlsysim.Models.Vision.ResNet50
_gpt2 = mlsysim.Models.Language.GPT2
_llama70b = mlsysim.Models.Language.Llama3_70B
_a100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.A100
_h100 = mlsysim.Hardware.Cloud.H100
_grids = mlsysim.Infrastructure.Grids

_p_a100_b1 = Engine.solve(model=_resnet, hardware=_a100, batch_size=1, precision="fp16")
_p_h100_b1 = Engine.solve(model=_resnet, hardware=_h100, batch_size=1, precision="fp16")
_p_a100_b256 = Engine.solve(model=_resnet, hardware=_a100, batch_size=256, precision="fp16")
_p_h100_b256 = Engine.solve(model=_resnet, hardware=_h100, batch_size=256, precision="fp16")
_speedup_b1 = (_p_a100_b1.latency / _p_h100_b1.latency).to("dimensionless").magnitude
_speedup_b256 = (_p_a100_b256.latency / _p_h100_b256.latency).to("dimensionless").magnitude

_ci_iowa = _grids.Iowa.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ci_quebec = _grids.Quebec.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ci_us = _grids.US_Avg.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_ci_poland = _grids.Poland.carbon_intensity_g_kwh
_iowa_quebec_ratio = _ci_iowa / _ci_quebec
_poland_quebec_ratio = _ci_poland / _ci_quebec

_kv_4k_gb = calc_kv_cache_size(
    n_layers=_llama70b.layers,
    n_heads=_llama70b.kv_heads,
    head_dim=_llama70b.hidden_dim // _llama70b.heads,
    seq_len=4096,
    batch_size=1,
    bytes_per_elem=2,
).to("GB").magnitude

_gpt2_params_b = _gpt2.parameters.to("Bparam").magnitude
_llama70b_params_b = _llama70b.parameters.to("Bparam").magnitude
_h100_flops = _h100.compute.peak_flops.to("TFLOPs/s").magnitude
_h100_bw = _h100.memory.bandwidth.to("TB/s").magnitude
_h100_ridge = (_h100.compute.peak_flops / _h100.memory.bandwidth).to("flop/byte").magnitude
```

MLSys·im provides a framework for assigning analytically grounded problem sets where every answer is deterministic and reproducible, regardless of the hardware students have access to. Combined with the companion [lecture slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/), it covers the tools needed for an ML systems course.

---

## Why MLSys·im for Teaching

| Challenge | How MLSys·im Helps |
|:----------|:------------------|
| Students lack GPU access | All analysis runs on a laptop, with no cloud credits needed |
| Homework answers vary by hardware | Vetted registry specs produce identical results everywhere |
| Hard to grade open-ended systems questions | Analytical solvers give deterministic, verifiable outputs |
| Specifications become stale | Registry updated from official datasheets; one update propagates everywhere |
| Students memorize without understanding | Analytical walkthroughs and parameter sweeps build genuine intuition |
| No time to build slides from scratch | Beamer lecture decks for Volumes I and II, with speaker notes, in-class exercises, and SVG diagrams |

---

## The Teaching Ecosystem

MLSys·im is one component of a larger open teaching toolkit:

| Resource | What It Provides | Link |
|:---------|:-----------------|:-----|
| **Textbook** | Four-volume open textbook: Volumes I and II online (Volume II as a preview), Volumes III and IV in preparation | [mlsysbook.ai](https://mlsysbook.ai) |
| **Lecture Slides** | Beamer lecture decks for Volumes I and II, with speaker notes on every slide | [Slides Portal](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/) |
| **MLSys·im** | Six primary workflows backed by typed resolver classes, a hardware registry, and deterministic assignments | [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) |
| **TinyML Courseware** | A four-course sequence of slide decks for embedded ML | [TinyML Slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/tinyml.html) |
| **Teaching Guide** | Semester plan, in-class activity types, and how to customize the decks | [Teaching Guide](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/teaching.html) |

## Course Integration Patterns

Map MLSys·im tutorials and assignments directly to textbook chapters and lecture decks. The table below shows one possible 16-week arrangement using Volume I slides.

| Week | Lecture Slides | Textbook Topic | MLSys·im Assignment |
|:-----|:---------------|:---------------|:-------------------|

| 5 | [NN Computation]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_05_nn_computation.pdf) | FLOPs, memory footprint | [Hello, Roofline](tutorials/00_hello_roofline.qmd): roofline analysis, batch size sweep |
| 8 | [Model Training]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_08_training.pdf) | Training memory budget | [Solver Guide](solver-guide.qmd): `TrainingMemoryModel`, ZeRO stages |

| 13 | [Model Serving]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_13_model_serving.pdf) | TTFT, ITL, KV-cache | [Two Phases of Inference](tutorials/02_two_phases.qmd): serving latency analysis |

### Pattern 2: Standalone Labs

Use individual tutorials as self-contained lab assignments in any systems course. Each tutorial is an executable walkthrough with live code and analytical verification:

| Tutorial | Duration | Key Concepts | Example `mlsysim` Output | Pairs With Slides |
|:---------|:---------|:-------------|:-------------------------|:------------------|
| [Hello, Roofline](tutorials/00_hello_roofline.qmd) | 15 min | Roofline model, memory vs. compute bound | A100 to H100 ResNet-50 speedup: `{python} f"{_speedup_b1:.2f}×"` (batch 1) vs. `{python} f"{_speedup_b256:.2f}×"` (batch 256) | [HW Acceleration]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_11_hw_acceleration.pdf) |
| [Geography is a Systems Variable](tutorials/07_geography.qmd) | 20 min | Energy, carbon footprint, regional grids | Iowa (`{python} f"{_ci_iowa:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`) vs. Quebec (`{python} f"{_ci_quebec:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`): `{python} f"{_iowa_quebec_ratio:.0f}×"` carbon gap | [Sustainable AI]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol2_15_sustainable_ai.pdf) |
| [Two Phases of Inference](tutorials/02_two_phases.qmd) | 25 min | TTFT vs. ITL, KV-cache pressure | Llama-3.1-70B KV-cache at 4K context: `{python} f"{_kv_4k_gb:.2f} GB"` per request | [Model Serving]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_13_model_serving.pdf) |
| [Scaling to 1000 GPUs](tutorials/06_scaling_1000_gpus.qmd) | 30 min | Data/tensor/pipeline parallelism | 3D parallelism scaling efficiency across cluster tiers | [Distributed Training]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol2_06_distributed_training.pdf) |

### Pattern 3: Capstone Projects

Advanced students compose multiple solvers to answer research-style questions. See [Writing a Custom Solver](solver-guide.qmd#writing-a-custom-solver) for the custom solver API.

## Assignment Ideas

### Homework: Hardware Comparison (30 min)

> Using `Engine.solve()`, compare ResNet-50 inference latency on the A100, H100, and Jetson AGX at batch sizes 1, 32, and 256. For each configuration, state whether the workload is memory-bound or compute-bound and explain why the bottleneck shifts with batch size.

**Pairs with**: [HW Acceleration slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_11_hw_acceleration.pdf) (roofline model, ridge point) and [Benchmarking slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_12_benchmarking.pdf) (measurement methodology).

### Homework: Training Memory Budget (30 min)

> Using `TrainingMemoryModel`, calculate the memory required to train GPT-2 (`{python} f"{_gpt2_params_b:.1f}B"` parameters) in FP16 with Adam optimizer under ZeRO Stage 0, Stage 1, and Stage 3. Explain *why* each stage reduces memory and what trade-off it introduces.

**Pairs with**: [Model Training slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_08_training.pdf) and [Distributed Training slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol2_06_distributed_training.pdf).

### Lab: Carbon-Aware Training (45 min)

> Using the SustainabilityModel, calculate the carbon footprint of training GPT-3 on a 256-GPU H100 cluster in Quebec (`{python} f"{_ci_quebec:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`) vs. US Average (`{python} f"{_ci_us:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`) vs. Poland (`{python} f"{_ci_poland:.0f} gCO₂/kWh"`, `{python} f"{_poland_quebec_ratio:.0f}×"` Quebec). Produce a table and a 2-paragraph analysis of why datacenter location matters more than hardware choice for carbon.

**Pairs with**: [Sustainable AI slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol2_15_sustainable_ai.pdf) (grid carbon intensity, PUE).

### Lab: LLM Serving Capacity Planning (45 min)

> Using the ServingModel, determine the maximum sequence length at which Llama-3.1-70B can serve a single request on an 8-GPU H100 node without exceeding memory. Then calculate TTFT and ITL at sequence lengths of 1K, 4K, and 16K tokens, and identify the sequence length at which KV-cache pressure dominates.

**Pairs with**: [Model Serving slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_13_model_serving.pdf) and [Inference at Scale slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol2_10_inference.pdf).

### Exam Question: Back-of-Envelope

> A GPU has `{python} f"{_h100_flops:.0f} TFLOP/s"` peak dense compute (FP16) and `{python} f"{_h100_bw:.2f} TB/s"` memory bandwidth. Compute (a) the ridge point in FLOP/Byte (`{python} f"{_h100_ridge:.0f} FLOP/Byte"`), (b) whether a model layer with arithmetic intensity of 50 FLOP/Byte is compute-bound or memory-bound, and (c) which regime a layer with arithmetic intensity of 400 FLOP/Byte occupies and what that implies about the benefit of moving to a GPU with 2× the bandwidth. Show all intermediate steps.

**Pairs with**: [HW Acceleration slides]({{< var slides_latest >}}/vol1_11_hw_acceleration.pdf) (roofline model, ridge point derivation).

### Capstone: Multi-Solver Design Study (1 week)

> Design a training cluster for a `{python} f"{_llama70b_params_b:.1f}B"`-parameter model. Use the DistributedModel to select a parallelism strategy, the EconomicsModel for TCO over 6 months, the SustainabilityModel to compare three datacenter locations, and the ReliabilityModel to determine checkpoint frequency. Present the analysis as a 3-page technical memo with quantitative justification for each decision.

**Pairs with**: the full [Volume II slide set](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/vol2.html), covering infrastructure, training, fault tolerance, and sustainability.

## Grading Notes

Because MLSys·im produces deterministic output from vetted specifications:

- **Answer keys are stable**: the same `mlsysim` version produces identical numbers for every student, every semester
- **Partial credit is straightforward**: grade the reasoning (which solver, which inputs, which bottleneck explanation), not only the number
- **Analytical predictions are easy to assess**: students can compute analytical bounds from the closed-form equations before running `mlsysim` to verify their work

::: {.callout-note}
## Version Pinning
Pin the exact version in the assignment instructions (`pip install mlsysim==<course-version>`) so answer keys remain valid even after new releases update specifications.
:::

---

## Reproducibility Guarantee

All specifications in the [MLSys Zoo](zoo/index.qmd) are:

- **Sourced** from official manufacturer datasheets and published benchmarks
- **Typed** with `pint.Quantity` for dimensional correctness, so unit errors are caught at runtime
- **Frozen** per release, so an exact pin such as `mlsysim==0.3.0` always produces the same answers

An answer key therefore works for every student, every semester.

---

## Jupyter & Quarto Compatibility

All tutorials run in:

- **Jupyter Notebooks**: standard `.ipynb` workflow
- **Quarto documents**: render to HTML, PDF, or slides with `quarto render`
- **Google Colab**: `pip install mlsysim` in the first cell, then run the tutorial

No GPU runtime required. CPU-only environments are sufficient because MLSys·im computes from equations, not from profiling.

---

## Getting Started

1. Point students to the [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) guide for installation
2. Assign the [Hello, Roofline](tutorials/00_hello_roofline.qmd) tutorial as a warmup
3. Browse the [Solver Guide](solver-guide.qmd) to select solvers for the course topics
4. Pair each assignment with the relevant [lecture slides](https://mlsysbook.ai/slides/) for classroom context
5. Use the [MLSys Zoo](zoo/index.qmd) for available hardware, model, and infrastructure specifications
